document.abstract: Terrestrial DTV transport stream management can be difficult at times. Broadcasters are now required to manage network-provided multiple-program standard-definition transport streams for multicast during part of the broadcast day, locally encoded content that can be added to the bouquet of MPTS services, and high-definition content. This paper explores the technical challenges of managing the complex bouquet of programs confronting the terrestrial DTV broadcaster, with a focus on how to switch programs in the ATSC transport stream.

authors.bio: Jean Macher joined Thales Broadcast & Multimedia in 1998 and relocated from France in 2000, taking on the role of digital television product line manager for the U.S. In France, he was in charge of the company's service information (SI) processing product line, and supervised the specification and adaptation of remultiplexing and SI processing products to U.S. markets. Macher previously worked as a project engineer for the company's U.K. Digital Terrestrial TV Project (remultiplexing and SI management for the BBC, CTI, On Digital), developing technical proposals and SI architecture specifications. He holds a Diploma of Engineering from the Superior Institute of Electrical Engineering of Paris (ISEP), a major French computer and electronic school (equivalent to an MSEE).
authors.name: Jean Macher

authors.bio: George F. Anderson III , is sales manager of digital services for Thales Broadcast & Multimedia. He started at Thales in January 2000 as sales manager for Comark Digital Systems (CDS), where his responsibilities included the promotion and sales of all the digital services necessary to interface the station's existing NTSC master control to high definition, SD and HD encoding, and datacasting capability, as well as to the station transmitter link distribution system. Anderson has many years of experience in broadcast sales and media management, including the movement of media both inter- and intra-facility, and providing media management solutions for the emerging digital media market, previously known as broadcast television. He holds a degree in electrical engineering with a minor in marketing from the University of Alabama. Anderson is a past Chair of the Philadelphia Section of SMPTE, and also served as Eastern Region Governor in 1999.
authors.name: George F. Anderson
